messages:
sara: heads up: offline replay 2064007890 shows a p99 spike for mixed-traffic when cost-aware-v2 kernel selector + continuous-batcher were on. traces uploaded to s3://redwood-sim/replays/2064007890/
andrew: can you paste the exact config used? wondering about token_budget_target and queue_policy.
sara: config snip:
```
kernel_selector: cost-aware-v2
continuous_batcher:
  enabled: true
  token_budget_target: 0.25
  queue_policy: fifo_weighted
kv_cache:
  prefetch: true
  warmup_ratio: 0.12
```
kevin: quick perf summary from the replay collector:
```
replay: 2064007890
baseline p99: 148ms -> this run p99: 189ms
gpu_wait_time +13.4ms
kernel_switch_overhead +8.1ms
kv_prefetch_wait +7.6ms
batch_coalesce_cost +5.1ms
```
maria: kernel_switch_overhead that big means we're switching kernels more frequently. token_budget_target=0.25 might be flushing too aggressively.
andrew: agreed. hypothesis: cost-aware-v2 picks small-stream kernels for 129-256 buckets which increases kernel churn when batches are single-stream heavy. two axes to try: raise token_budget_target or bias kernel selector toward fused kernels. also test a small fifo grace window to allow coalescing.
sara: I'm going to enqueue three A/B replay variants: A) token_budget_target=0.38, B) keep 0.25 but kernel_selector=stable-fused-prefer, C) 0.25 + fifo_grace_ms=6. will attach kernel_switch trace and disable prefetch for one sub-run to isolate KV impact.
andrew: queued: replay/2064007922 (A), replay/2064007936 (B), replay/2064007948 (C) — sim-bot will post brief summaries. also added header trace: kernel_switch_event=true and metric parsing hook kernel_switches_per_1k_tokens.
sim-bot: job queued: replay/2064007922 (A) / replay/2064007936 (B) / replay/2064007948 (C) ✅
kevin: snapshot of batch demographics from the problematic run:
``
<=32: 11%
33-128: 51%
129-256: 30%
>256: 8%
avg tokens/batch: 298
avg streams/batch: 2.9
```
sara: small-short streams (~<=32) aren't dominant but we see many 1-stream-256 batches which force the less-efficient kernel path.
maria: another idea: soft-aggregation where the batcher uses a small grace window to wait for coalescing streams up to X ms but still honor p50 budgets. that's the fifo_grace_ms test.
andrew: replay results in:
- replay/2064007922 (A): token_budget_target=0.38 => p99 156ms (baseline 148ms), kernel_switches_per_1k=1.7, cost +1.5%
- replay/2064007936 (B): fused-prefer selector => p99 150ms, kernel_switches_per_1k=1.2, cost +3.1%
- replay/2064007948 (C): fifo_grace_ms=6 => p99 152ms, kernel_switches_per_1k=1.4, cost +1.8%
andrew: also ran a small variation D: token_budget=0.33 + fifo_grace_ms=4 => replay/2064007955 => p99 149ms, kernel_switches_per_1k=1.35, cost +1.4%.
kevin: useful numbers. takeaways: increasing token budget reduces kernel churn but costs a bit; fused kernels reduce churn the most but at higher cost; grace window gets most of the p99 improvements at modest cost.
sara: proposed rollout: codify policy as token_budget_target=0.33, fifo_grace_ms=4, kernel_selector: priority_rules: - if avg_streams>3 prefer fused else cost-aware-v2. start canary 5% on Dedicated for 24h. auto-rollback if p99 > baseline + 12% or cost > baseline + 9%.
maria: add instrumentation: kernel_switches_per_1k_tokens, kv_prefetch_wait, batch_coalesce_latency. add alert on kernel_switches_per_1k > 2.0 sustained for 5m. also upload a small eval harness that runs 50 fixed prompts to check parity.
andrew: I'm drafting the PR with config diffs and replay artifacts at s3://redwood-sim/replays/20640079xx/. will include parsed CSVs and the kernel switch trace.
sim-bot: replay artifacts available: s3://redwood-sim/replays/20640079xx/artifacts.tar.gz ✅
sara: thanks. maria, kevin — could one of you own the rollout monitoring and incident runbook? ops-bot: noting to tie rollback into incident orchestration if thresholds breach.
kevin: i'll own monitoring for the canary. i'll wire the kernel_switch metric to the perf dashboard and create a simple alert.
maria: i'll own eval parity harness and KV hit-rate checks. will create a short test suite and make sure prefetch toggles are visible per-host.
sara: nice. follow-ups: (1) PR for config change, (2) small canary, (3) collect metrics & decide on wider rollout after 24h. closing for now, will post PR link when ready. cc @product-infra
